title: Beyond Local Surprise: Grounded Dialogue as Selective Belief Revision under Referential Uncertainty
abstract: arXiv:2608.26035v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a speaker refers to a scene that the listener cannot directly see, the listener must decide whether to preserve its current understanding or revise it as new utterances arrive. Many language systems treat local mismatch as a cue for updating: divergence from the current understanding encourages adjustment. Yet conversational understanding may be more conservative, interpreting mismatching evidence relative to prior understanding rather than immediately revising it. We introduce a controlled, data-driven framework for turn-by-turn preserve/revise decisions in dialogue, where competing revision policies are learned under otherwise identical conditions. We compare four theory-driven revision strategies, each reflecting a different assumption about when listeners should preserve or revise. Two findings stand out. translated_title: 超越局部意外：在指称不确定性下作为选择性信念修正的情境化对话
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26035v1 公告类型：新 摘要：当说话者指代一个听者无法直接看到的场景时，听者必须决定是保持当前理解，还是随着新话语的到来而修正它。许多语言系统将局部不匹配视为更新的线索：与当前理解的偏差会促使调整。然而，对话理解可能更为保守，将不匹配的证据相对于先前理解进行解释，而非立即修正。我们引入了一个受控的、数据驱动的框架，用于对话中逐轮保持/修正决策，其中竞争性的修正策略在相同条件下学习。我们比较了四种理论驱动的修正策略，每种策略反映了关于听者何时应保持或修正的不同假设。两个发现尤为突出。首先，一种仅基于局部偏差更新的不匹配驱动策略，对不匹配反应强烈，但会破坏对话的稳定性。
tldr: 本文提出一个数据驱动框架，比较四种对话信念修正策略，发现仅依赖局部不匹配的更新策略虽反应敏感但破坏稳定性，强调对话理解应更保守地结合先前理解。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a data-driven framework comparing four belief-revision strategies in dialogue, finding that mismatch-driven updating reacts strongly but destabilizes conversation, advocating for more conservative interpretation grounded in prior understanding.
